boundary: Evidence-request preparation, not an assessment. A requirement names documents a researcher would need; it does not state that those documents exist, that any product meets the requirement, or that any dependency is approved. User-recorded statuses stay in the browser and are never validation: a received document has not been reviewed, authenticated or found sufficient.

evidence_categories.specification: A vendor or standards document stating what a product is specified to be
evidence_categories.design_documentation: A design, architecture or method document
evidence_categories.qualification_record: A record that a part met an accelerator maker's qualification criteria
evidence_categories.production_record: Evidence of volume production of a named combination
evidence_categories.procurement_record: A contract, purchase or delivery record
evidence_categories.installation_record: A dated record of installation at a named site
evidence_categories.test_record: Test procedures with criteria and results
evidence_categories.operational_record: Monitoring records over a stated period
evidence_categories.measurement: A measured result with method and conditions
evidence_categories.regulatory_determination: Rule text and a classification or licence determination for a named transaction

basis_definitions.source_derived: The requirement follows from reviewed primary sources and the findings listed with it
basis_definitions.analytical_recommendation: This project's recommendation where reviewed sources are silent; no source supports it directly

availability_definitions.published: The reviewed sources publish the requested information
availability_definitions.partially_published: The reviewed sources publish part of it, or it is published with unresolved conflicts
availability_definitions.not_published: No reviewed source publishes it; it would have to be requested

workflows.title: HBM4 integration evidence request
workflows.research_question: What documentary evidence would be required to substantiate the integration and qualification of named HBM4 memory in a specific AI accelerator package?
workflows.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: HBM4 interface standard and revision
requirements.document_requested: The normative JEDEC JESD270-4 text (and any revision, such as JESD270-4A) that the memory and the accelerator's memory controller are designed to
requirements.why_it_matters: The interface defines width, channels and signalling. JEDEC's public announcement is not the normative text, and the revision in use decides which speed bins and timing apply.
acceptance_considerations: Names the exact document number and revision
States the speed bins and voltage options used
limitations: The normative text is distributed by JEDEC and was not reviewed by this project
requirements.permits_after_review: Which interface parameters the integration must meet
requirements.not_established_without_review: That any named part or package conforms to the standard
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Named memory part and configuration
requirements.document_requested: The supplier part number with capacity, stack height (12-high or 16-high), die density and per-stack bandwidth for the stack actually integrated
requirements.why_it_matters: Suppliers announce several HBM4 configurations. An integration claim needs the specific part, because capacity, height and speed differ between them.
acceptance_considerations: Issued by the memory supplier or the accelerator maker
Ties the part number to the named accelerator
limitations: Supplier announcements give configurations, not which part a given accelerator uses
requirements.permits_after_review: Which stack configuration the package carries
requirements.not_established_without_review: That the named part is qualified in the accelerator
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Qualified speed grade on the named accelerator
requirements.document_requested: The pin rate and per-stack bandwidth at which the accelerator maker qualified the named stack, with the test conditions
requirements.why_it_matters: Supplier pin rates (over 10, 11 or 11.7 Gb/s) exceed JEDEC's announced 8 Gb/s. A conforming interface does not fix the speed the package actually runs.
requirements.technical_scope: Per stack, on one accelerator platform
acceptance_considerations: States pin rate, temperature and voltage conditions
Comes from the accelerator maker's qualification, not a supplier press release
limitations: No reviewed source discloses a qualified speed grade for a named HBM4 accelerator
requirements.permits_after_review: The bandwidth the integrated memory is specified to deliver
requirements.not_established_without_review: That supplier-announced pin rates apply to the integrated part
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Base logic die implementation
requirements.document_requested: The base-die process node and fabricating foundry for the qualified stack
requirements.why_it_matters: Every HBM4 stack sits on a logic base die. Its process and foundry are a manufacturing dependency separate from the DRAM process.
acceptance_considerations: Names the node and the fabricating entity for the stack in question
limitations: SK hynix and Micron do not state the node for their HBM4 base dies
requirements.permits_after_review: Which logic manufacturing capability the stack depends on
requirements.not_established_without_review: That the stated arrangement applies to every shipped stack
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Stack assembly method
requirements.document_requested: The bonding and underfill method (for example MR-MUF or hybrid bonding) used for the qualified stack height
requirements.why_it_matters: Assembly method affects warpage, heat removal and the stack heights that can be built; 16-high stacks raise thermal questions.
acceptance_considerations: Identifies the method for the specific part, not the supplier's roadmap
limitations: Hybrid bonding is described for future HBM and is not stated as used in HBM4
requirements.permits_after_review: How the stack was assembled
requirements.not_established_without_review: Thermal or reliability performance of the stack in a package
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Package integration technology
requirements.document_requested: The interposer or bridge technology (for example a named CoWoS variant), interposer size and HBM stack count for the named accelerator package
requirements.why_it_matters: Interposer size bounds how many stacks fit beside the logic dies. Foundry roadmaps describe capability, not the package of a named HBM4 product.
acceptance_considerations: Issued by the accelerator maker or the packaging provider
Names the product, not a technology family
limitations: No reviewed source names the package of any named HBM4 accelerator
TSMC states the 5.5-reticle CoWoS-L status two ways
requirements.permits_after_review: Which packaging route the integration depends on
requirements.not_established_without_review: That a roadmap size is in production for the product
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Substrate and assembly provider
requirements.document_requested: The organic substrate supplier and the assembly and test sites for the package
requirements.why_it_matters: Substrate and assembly are separable industrial stages; the reviewed disclosures name them only as categories.
acceptance_considerations: Names suppliers and sites for the specific product
limitations: Substrate and assembly providers for named packages are not disclosed in the reviewed sources
requirements.permits_after_review: Which suppliers and sites the package depends on
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Known-good-stack test documentation
requirements.document_requested: The test flow showing how stacks are tested before integration and who performs it
requirements.why_it_matters: Integration yield depends on testing stacks before they are placed; the reviewed sources do not describe the flow.
acceptance_considerations: States test coverage, the testing party and the stage at which tests run
limitations: Analytical request: no reviewed source documents the flow
requirements.permits_after_review: Where defective stacks are screened
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Power and thermal integration data
requirements.document_requested: Stack power at the qualified speed grade and the package thermal design for the HBM stacks
requirements.why_it_matters: Suppliers state efficiency gains against differing baselines; package-level heat removal for the named configuration is not stated.
acceptance_considerations: Gives absolute power, not only percentage gains
States the operating point
limitations: Supplier efficiency figures use different baselines and cannot be compared directly
requirements.permits_after_review: The thermal load the package must remove
requirements.not_established_without_review: Operating temperatures in a deployed system
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Accelerator maker's integration statement
requirements.document_requested: A statement by the accelerator maker naming the memory generation, stack count and package technology of the product
requirements.why_it_matters: Product-level disclosures are the closest public evidence of integration. AMD's MI300X disclosure shows the form, but it covers HBM3, not HBM4.
acceptance_considerations: Issued by the accelerator maker
Names memory generation, stack count and package technology together
limitations: MI300X evidence is HBM3 and does not transfer to HBM4 products
NVIDIA states on-package HBM4 for Rubin without naming suppliers or package variant
requirements.permits_after_review: What the product integrates, as its maker states it
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Qualification test results and acceptance criteria
requirements.document_requested: The accelerator maker's qualification report for the named stack: tests run, acceptance thresholds and results
requirements.why_it_matters: Supplier statements that HBM4 is 'designed for' a platform stop short of qualification, which is the accelerator maker's decision.
requirements.technical_scope: Per supplier part on one accelerator platform
acceptance_considerations: States criteria and results, not only that qualification occurred
Dated and tied to a part number
limitations: No qualification record for a named HBM4 accelerator was reviewed
requirements.permits_after_review: That the named part met the maker's criteria at the stated time
requirements.not_established_without_review: That another supplier's part could replace it
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Production integration evidence
requirements.document_requested: Evidence that the named memory and package combination is in volume production for the named accelerator
requirements.why_it_matters: Supplier 'mass production' statements are not product-specific, and accelerator production statements do not name memory suppliers.
acceptance_considerations: Names the product, the supplier and the production stage together
limitations: Supplier production stages and accelerator production statements are separate disclosures
requirements.permits_after_review: That the named combination is produced at volume
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

requirements.title: Additional-supplier qualification evidence
requirements.document_requested: Qualification evidence for each additional supplier claimed for the same accelerator
requirements.why_it_matters: Two suppliers stating their HBM4 is designed for the same platform does not establish that the platform is multi-sourced.
acceptance_considerations: One qualification record per supplier and part
limitations: Design-target statements are not qualification
requirements.permits_after_review: That more than one supplier's part passed the accelerator maker's qualification
requirements.not_established_without_review: That either part can replace the other in supply
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that separate an interface standard and supplier announcements from product-specific integration and qualification.

workflows.title: Accelerator bandwidth comparison evidence request
workflows.research_question: What evidence is required before comparing memory and interconnect performance between two accelerator systems?
workflows.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: System identification and generation
requirements.document_requested: The exact product, SKU, generation and configuration for each system being compared
requirements.why_it_matters: Vendors publish different figures for different products (for example Rubin on HGX and on Vera Rubin NVL72). A comparison needs the configuration fixed first.
acceptance_considerations: Names product, generation and configuration
Dated
limitations: MI300X (CDNA 3, HBM3) and Rubin (HBM4) are different generations
requirements.permits_after_review: Which figures apply to which system
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Memory configuration
requirements.document_requested: Memory type, stack count, capacity and interface width for each accelerator
requirements.why_it_matters: Per-accelerator bandwidth is the sum over stacks; stack count and width must be known to interpret it.
acceptance_considerations: States stack count rather than leaving it to inference
limitations: NVIDIA does not state Rubin's stack count; eight stacks is an inference from 288 GB
requirements.permits_after_review: How the aggregate figure is built
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Per-stack peak bandwidth basis
requirements.document_requested: The interface width and pin rate behind each per-stack bandwidth figure
requirements.why_it_matters: Per-stack peak is width times pin rate divided by eight; without both, a figure cannot be checked.
acceptance_considerations: States width and pin rate
limitations: Peak arithmetic, not sustained bandwidth
requirements.permits_after_review: That per-stack figures are arithmetically consistent
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Per-accelerator memory bandwidth with dated source
requirements.document_requested: The vendor's current specification of per-accelerator memory bandwidth, with its date and basis
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA publishes 22 TB/s (January and July posts, HGX page) and 19.2 TB/s (November post, Vera Rubin NVL72 page) per Rubin GPU, unexplained.
acceptance_considerations: Dated, versioned specification document
States whether the figure is peak and which configuration it applies to
limitations: The Rubin conflict is unresolved; either figure must carry its date and source
requirements.permits_after_review: Which figure the vendor specifies for the configuration compared
requirements.not_established_without_review: Which of two conflicting vendor figures is correct
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Per-link bandwidth and direction
requirements.document_requested: Per-link bandwidth, direction convention and encoding for each scale-up link
requirements.why_it_matters: A bidirectional figure is twice a per-direction one. AMD states 128 GB/s bidirectional per MI300X link; NVIDIA's direction conventions vary by document.
acceptance_considerations: States direction and whether the figure is raw or after encoding
limitations: Encoding and effective link bandwidth are not stated by AMD
requirements.permits_after_review: The link rate and its direction convention
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Per-GPU scale-up aggregate and its scope
requirements.document_requested: A vendor statement of each scale-up aggregate figure's scope: per link, per GPU or per platform
requirements.why_it_matters: AMD labels 896 GB/s a ring-of-8 aggregate without stating per-GPU scope; NVIDIA states NVLink 6 per Rubin GPU as 3.6 TB/s and 3 TB/s. Neither pair can be compared until scope is stated.
acceptance_considerations: States scope explicitly rather than by label
Dated and versioned
limitations: A reported 2025 CDNA 4 edition stating per-GPU scope is pending version verification and is not evidence here
NVIDIA's 3.6 and 3 TB/s figures remain unexplained
requirements.permits_after_review: Which aggregate figures are like-for-like
requirements.not_established_without_review: Relative fabric capability or achieved throughput
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Scale-up topology
requirements.document_requested: The topology of each scale-up domain: direct mesh or switched, domain size and links per GPU
requirements.why_it_matters: A fully connected eight-GPU mesh and a 72-GPU switched domain distribute bandwidth differently; aggregates mean different things in each.
acceptance_considerations: States domain size and switching
limitations: Topology describes paths, not achieved throughput
requirements.permits_after_review: How aggregate figures relate to peer-to-peer paths
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Host and CPU link specification
requirements.document_requested: Host link type, lane count, rate and direction convention for each accelerator
requirements.why_it_matters: Raw x16 PCIe and CXL totals count both directions unless stated; NVIDIA does not say its 256 GB/s figure uses the same basis.
acceptance_considerations: States direction and raw or payload basis
limitations: Whether MI300X or Rubin implement CXL is not established
requirements.permits_after_review: The host link capacity on a stated basis
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Scale-out bandwidth per GPU
requirements.document_requested: Per-GPU scale-out bandwidth with units (bits or bytes) and direction
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's 1.6 Tb/s per GPU is in bits with no direction; scale-up and scale-out figures differ by an order of magnitude and in dependency model.
acceptance_considerations: States units and direction
limitations: Direction of the 1.6 Tb/s figure is not stated
requirements.permits_after_review: Scale-out capacity on a stated basis
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Measurement method and test conditions
requirements.document_requested: For any measured figure: the test program or measurement procedure, message sizes, number of GPUs, topology and the measuring party
requirements.why_it_matters: Every figure in the reviewed sources is a peak; a defensible performance comparison needs measured values under stated conditions.
acceptance_considerations: Method, conditions and measuring party are stated
Raw results are available
limitations: No measured collective or application bandwidth was reviewed for either system
requirements.permits_after_review: Achieved throughput under the stated conditions
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Workload and software configuration
requirements.document_requested: Driver, communication library and framework versions, and the workload used, for each measurement
requirements.why_it_matters: Achieved bandwidth depends on software as well as hardware; results without versions cannot be reproduced or compared.
acceptance_considerations: Versions and workload are recorded with the result
limitations: Analytical request: no reviewed source provides such records
requirements.permits_after_review: That two measurements used comparable software
requirements.not_established_without_review: That results transfer to other software versions
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Reproducibility evidence
requirements.document_requested: Repeated runs with variance, and the raw data or scripts needed to reproduce each measurement
requirements.why_it_matters: A single figure without variance cannot support a comparison between systems.
acceptance_considerations: Run count, variance and raw data are provided
limitations: Analytical request
requirements.permits_after_review: How stable a measured result is
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

requirements.title: Rack aggregates versus per-GPU figures
requirements.document_requested: The vendor's statement of how each rack-level aggregate relates to per-GPU figures
requirements.why_it_matters: GB200 NVL72's 130 TB/s is a rack aggregate; comparing it with a per-GPU figure mixes scopes.
acceptance_considerations: States both the aggregate and the per-GPU basis
limitations: Rack aggregate and per-GPU figures are different scopes and, here, different generations
requirements.permits_after_review: How rack and per-GPU figures relate
requirements.objective: Collect the documents that fix each figure's unit, direction, scope, basis and measurement before any comparison is drawn.

workflows.title: AI rack deployment evidence request
workflows.research_question: Which documentary records are necessary to move from a published AI rack specification to a defensible statement about installation, commissioning, and operation?
workflows.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Rack hardware configuration
requirements.document_requested: The bill of materials for the rack as delivered: compute trays, switch trays, power shelves, bus bar and manifolds
requirements.why_it_matters: The vendor's rack description is the specification every later record refers to; the delivered configuration may differ.
acceptance_considerations: Lists components by part number for the specific rack
limitations: The user guide covers GB200 and GB300 together
requirements.permits_after_review: What the rack is specified to contain
requirements.not_established_without_review: That any rack was delivered or installed
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Scalable-unit design
requirements.document_requested: The facility design for the scalable unit, with its power budget broken down
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's 1.2 MW per eight-rack unit is a design figure; eight racks at about 120 kW leave 0.24 MW unitemised.
acceptance_considerations: Itemises the 1.2 MW
States the tested scale unambiguously
limitations: A design value, not measured consumption
requirements.permits_after_review: What the facility was designed to supply
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Power redundancy design and verification
requirements.document_requested: The vendor's power-shelf specification stating the redundancy scheme, and a site test verifying it
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's user guide says N+N and its reference architecture says N; redundancy cannot be inferred from installed PSU capacity.
acceptance_considerations: States the scheme and the usable capacity under it
A failover test record for the site
limitations: The vendor documents conflict; neither is chosen here
requirements.permits_after_review: The intended scheme, then whether a site verified it
requirements.not_established_without_review: That the rack survives a shelf failure
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Bus bar topology and rating
requirements.document_requested: The rack power-distribution specification: bus-bar paths, current rating and the voltage at which it applies
requirements.why_it_matters: A 1,400 A bus bar at about 50 V is about 70 kW against an approximately 120 kW rack; the path count is not published.
acceptance_considerations: States paths, rating and voltage
limitations: The path count is not inferred from arithmetic
requirements.permits_after_review: How the rack's DC distribution carries its load
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Cooling and facility interface specification
requirements.document_requested: Coolant type, flow, supply temperature, pressure and liquid-cooling class, and the liquid and air heat split
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA documents liquid cooling through cold plates but states none of these parameters; generic data-centre classes do not substitute.
acceptance_considerations: Issued by the vendor for this product
States each parameter with units
limitations: The flow arithmetic on the reference page is illustrative, not a product requirement
requirements.permits_after_review: What the facility loop must provide
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Firmware and software baseline
requirements.document_requested: The required firmware set and software versions for the rack, with the documentation edition they come from
requirements.why_it_matters: Firmware spans compute trays, switches and power shelves; orchestration support differs between documentation editions.
acceptance_considerations: Names versions and the documentation edition
limitations: Support statements are version-scoped and do not show deployment
requirements.permits_after_review: Which baseline a rack should run
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Site electrical capacity
requirements.document_requested: The utility supply agreement, single-line diagram and available capacity at the site
requirements.why_it_matters: A rack's rated draw is not the capacity a site can deliver; available capacity is shown only by site records.
requirements.technical_scope: Per named site and utility connection
acceptance_considerations: Names the site and states available capacity and redundancy
limitations: No site record was reviewed
requirements.permits_after_review: What electrical capacity was contracted for the site
requirements.not_established_without_review: That it is energised or sufficient under load
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Procurement and delivery records
requirements.document_requested: Purchase and delivery records naming the racks, quantities and site
requirements.why_it_matters: Product availability does not show delivery to any site.
acceptance_considerations: Names site, quantity and date
limitations: No procurement record was reviewed
requirements.permits_after_review: That equipment was procured for a site
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Installation records
requirements.document_requested: Installation records for each rack at the site
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's checklist names installation items, but a blank checklist is not a record.
requirements.technical_scope: Per rack at a named site
acceptance_considerations: Dated, names the site and the racks
limitations: Installation does not establish commissioning
requirements.permits_after_review: That racks were installed
requirements.not_established_without_review: That they were commissioned or operate
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Network integration records
requirements.document_requested: The NVLink domain configuration and north-south network installation records for the rack
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA advises bringing up NVLink switches first and installing north-south switches before deployment; procedures are not records.
acceptance_considerations: A dated record for the named site
limitations: The reviewed documents are procedures, not records
requirements.permits_after_review: That the networks were configured as documented
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Commissioning procedure and results
requirements.document_requested: Commissioning test results for power, cooling, network and compute subsystems, with dates
requirements.why_it_matters: Bring-up checks and validation tests are described by NVIDIA, but their results at a site are what commissioning evidence consists of.
acceptance_considerations: Results for each subsystem with dates
limitations: Test descriptions are not results
requirements.permits_after_review: That subsystems passed their commissioning tests
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Acceptance criteria and test results
requirements.document_requested: The acceptance criteria with thresholds, and the integrated acceptance test results
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's checklist names items such as 'thermal management validated under load' without thresholds.
acceptance_considerations: Thresholds are stated before results
Signed by the responsible parties
limitations: No thresholds are published in the reviewed sources
requirements.permits_after_review: That the integrated configuration met stated criteria
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Operational monitoring records
requirements.document_requested: Monitoring records over a stated period: power draw, temperatures, leak events and availability
requirements.why_it_matters: NVIDIA describes leak events collated in its cluster software and coordinated with building management; records show whether this operates.
acceptance_considerations: Covers a stated period
Names the site
limitations: No operating record was reviewed
requirements.permits_after_review: How the installation behaved over the period
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Workload-level measured performance
requirements.document_requested: Measured performance of named workloads on the installation, with configuration and method
requirements.why_it_matters: An installed software stack shows components are present, not that the cluster performs.
acceptance_considerations: Method, configuration and workload stated
limitations: No measured result was reviewed
requirements.permits_after_review: Achieved performance for the stated workload
requirements.objective: Collect records for each stage from specified to operationally observed, without treating any stage as implying the next.

requirements.title: Access and regulatory documentation
requirements.document_requested: The classification of the items, the applicable rule provisions and any licence or exception determination for the named transaction
requirements.why_it_matters: Only BIS's 2024 announcement and two current eCFR sections (742.6, 740.25) were reviewed; other provisions may apply, and applicability is transaction-specific.

Prepared by qualified counsel

This workbench gives no legal view

requirements.not_established_without_review: How any transaction is classified or licensed
